newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade thin at $65 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade thin at $65 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $65.00 per cwt in light volume, down $1.00 from thin sales Friday and Tuesday, feedlot sources said.
About 2,100 slaughter steers and heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in Kansas and about 1,500 sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area.
Other bids at $65.00 were passed by owners asking $67.00, steady with last week's top price.
Many cattle owners resisted attempts to push prices below $66.00 amid belief that feedlots were current enough to wait another day to see if beef demand improves.

There was concern that wet, cool weather in the central U.S. had slowed beef consumption during the Memorial Day holiday weekend. Industry sources said it could take a few days to gauge how well beef moved during the holiday.

Beef prices were quoted lower at midday, but movement was greater than a week ago. Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.23 to $0.69 per cwt, with 247 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. Fabricated beef movement for the entire day a week ago was 240 loads.
Attempts to nurture steady fed cattle prices were overshadowed by ideas packers had adequate cattle supplies.
